Class-block development reduces five-class P 157652.780547→49807.068440 and three-class 198645.509041→134043.712499; single-class is 0.01 worse and CP-SAT is much more expensive. findings.evidence_level: Middle supported; additional localized higher-layer intervention evidence
findings.basis: Saved costs/ledger support greater sailing spending with far lower alpha penalties, not a free reduction of every objective component. Five-class loading loss632→35, P1 shortage512→8, P2 185→90. Three-class port3 shortage230→0 while loading loss844→498. Original raw independently supports the P1 capacity example: service at t3 gives372>336, t4 gives348, t5 gives324; initial ship availability3/cargo300 is a genuine timing/storage interaction. Actual class-pair feasible improvement while other class arcs are fixed supplies a localized intervention, beyond a cost list.
findings.limits_or_missing: No route-specific ablation identifies each voyage as necessary, and no one vessel is established as the sole cause of the total gain. Raw alpha is legal priced slack; avoidable incumbent slack is not inevitable physical unmet demand. Terminal exits are service at their origin, not future delivery.
